main.title: Donkey Kong Bananza
main.summary: Donkey Kong Bananza is a 2025 platform game developed by Nintendo EPD for the Nintendo Switch 2.

cards.heading: Breaking a path towards the planetary core
cards.text: Donkey Kong Bananza is a 2025 platform game developed by Nintendo EPD for the Nintendo Switch 2.  The player controls the gorilla Donkey Kong, who ventures to the planetary core with the teenage Pauline. Similar to EPD's Super Mario Odyssey (2017), the player explores sandbox-like levels while completing objectives, battling enemies, and collecting objects. Bananza is distinguished by its destructible environments; the player can destroy most terrain to create paths and find items. They upgrade Donkey Kong's abilities by collecting banana-shaped diamonds and obtaining power-up transformations.

cards.heading: Donkey Kong’s strength meets voxel technology
cards.text: EPD began working on Donkey Kong Bananza following Super Mario Odyssey's completion, following a request from the manager Yoshiaki Koizumi. It was the first internally-developed Donkey Kong game since Donkey Kong Jungle Beat (2004), and Koizumi and Donkey Kong's creator Shigeru Miyamoto provided input. EPD wanted to honor Donkey Kong's past while establishing a new direction. They made greater use of the voxel technology that allowed players to manipulate terrain in some Odyssey levels, with large, destructible worlds emphasizing Donkey Kong's strength. The development began on the original Nintendo Switch, but shifted to the Switch 2 due to technical constraints.

cards.heading: A return to three-dimensional platforming
cards.text: Nintendo released Donkey Kong Bananza on July 17, 2025, following a marketing campaign that included Nintendo Direct presentations, demo exhibitions, and live service game events. It was the first original Donkey Kong game since Donkey Kong Country: Tropical Freeze (2014) and the first 3D platformer since Donkey Kong 64 (1999). Bananza received acclaim; critics considered it the Switch 2's killer app and praised its visuals, gameplay, level design, and story, but criticized the camera and frame rate. As of June 30, 2026, it had sold 4.78 million copies, making it the second best-selling Switch 2 game. It was one of the highest-rated games of 2025 and was nominated for numerous accolades, including Game of the Year.

main.title: Drag x Drive
main.subtitle: Two mouse controls drive two wheels
main.summary: Drag x Drive is Nintendo's three-on-three sports game, released for Nintendo Switch 2 on 14 August 2025.

cards.heading: Two mouse controls drive two wheels
cards.text: Drag x Drive is Nintendo's three-on-three sports game, released for Nintendo Switch 2 on 14 August 2025. Players control robotic competitors in wheelchair-like vehicles and attempt to score in the opposing basket. Its distinctive control scheme uses both Joy-Con 2 controllers as mice, assigning one to each wheel. Movement therefore comes from the coordination of the player's hands: sliding both forward drives ahead, while moving one differently turns the vehicle towards another route through the court.

cards.heading: A basketball match performed with the hands
cards.text: Shooting changes the gesture from propulsion to a raised hand and flick of the wrist. A player must first create a useful position, then shift from driving to aiming before a defender closes the space. Raising an arm also signals for a pass, and opponents can challenge possession or block a shot. The controls make basic teamwork physical. Reaching open ground, asking for the ball and attempting a basket each require a different movement rather than a separate abstract command alone.

cards.heading: The edge of the court becomes a ramp
cards.text: Half-pipes surround the court, letting competitors launch into tricks and dunks above the ordinary playing surface. Practice against computer-controlled opponents provides time to learn the relationship between wheel movement and positioning before online matches. Sayako Doi composed the music. Drag x Drive uses a compact sport to demonstrate the Switch 2's dual mouse input, building the contest around the effort of steering, turning and shooting with the same two hands that give the player's vehicle its momentum.
